name: uudeview
why: Decoding uuencoded multi-part posts is a fossil of Usenet-era encodings, a door into old file transport formats worth a look.

brief.what_it_is: UUDeview is a command-line decoder that takes saved email or newsgroup articles, including multi-part and multi-file posts, and extracts the binary files inside them. It auto-detects the encoding (uuencoding, xxencoding, MIME Base64, BinHex, and later yEnc) and writes out the decoded files. The package also includes UUEnview, which runs the other way and encodes files for mail or news, and both tools sit on a shared C library. It does not do file compression or encryption, and the author says it is not needed for ordinary web downloads.
brief.why_it_exists: The author wrote it in the Usenet era, when attachments in mail and newsgroups were split across several articles and had to be concatenated by hand before the standard uudecode utility could handle them. The page frames it as a decoder built for newsreader users who want to save a batch of articles and let the tool sort out the rest.
brief.how_it_works: You save a set of articles from your mail client or newsreader into one or more files and run UUDeview on them. It reads the subject headers to work out the correct order of parts, detects each part's encoding, and decodes the files within. The author says it was built around an earlier tool, uunconc, and extended with heuristics for mangled or out-of-order input, which is why it is described as 'smart'.

commands_seen.context: UUDeview option: 'Autoclear'. Deletes every input file if anything was decoded from it. The author warns it does not check whether a file held other undecodable data.
UUDeview option: autorename. If an output file exists, it becomes foo.gif.1.
UUDeview option: inserts a unique sequential number before the extension, so foo.gif becomes foo.1.gif.
UUDeview option: 'more mime' mode, which searches MIME messages less aggressively and avoids some false readings.
UUEnview option: encodes the input as plain text, mainly useful with -a for text attachments.
UUEnview option: encodes the input as quoted-printable.
UUEnview option: sets the From: header on mail or news it sends.
UUEnview option: sets the Reply-To: header on mail or news it sends.

brief.install_notes: The old homepage offers a Unix source distribution (uudeview-0.5.20.tar.gz, about 250kB, or a .zip, or a self-installing uudeview-sfx-0.5.20.sh), with an Installation Manual linked from the page. The Unix build gives the uudeview and uuenview command-line tools, and xdeview is installed only if Tcl/Tk is present. A Windows console build is a MinGW port of the Unix tools and must be run from a console, not Explorer. A DOS build is available but old. The page says the Macintosh version runs in the macOS console using the Unix instructions, with no GUI. None of this is a Homebrew-specific step. Configuration can come from the $UUDEVIEW and $UUENVIEW environment variables.
brief.standout: It is a decoder built around the messy reality of real posts: it reconstructs part order from subject headers and keeps adding special-case heuristics, and its library has been embedded in KMail and WinZip. The history section is also an unusually candid account of a rewrite that was abandoned.
brief.status: Quiet, with the old homepage marked obsolete. The page was last modified in March 2004. It says the last official release was 0.5.13 in January 1997 and that the 0.5.15 release in June 2001 came after a four-year dormancy. Its download section lists 0.5.20 for Unix, and the author says there are no promises about future versions beyond possible bugfix releases. The page redirects users to a GitHub repository for a more recent version, but I could not reach it. I tried one guessed GitHub URL, which returned 404, so I cannot confirm the current state of that project.
brief.caveats: The old homepage warns that the versions it hosts are ancient, have unfixed issues, and may have unsafe buffer overflows, so use the GitHub version it points to instead. The -c autoclear option can delete files that contain other data. yEnc is incompatible with MIME, and the author discourages it. The library is GPL rather than LGPL, so it can only be linked into software under a GPL-compatible license. The Windows and DOS builds are old or console-only, and there is no GUI on macOS. xdeview needs Tcl/Tk. The author provides no support.
quotes: UUDeview is a particularly powerful decoder. It was designed to fit the needs of news readers.
Support for UUDeview is not available unless you give me a really good reason for it.
